mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses equity discount rates and increases risk appetite, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors shift from fixed income to equities.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 8.0% signals severe labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 8.0 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate collapsing consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as recession risks intensify.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both decline for 2 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 100 (INDPRO < 100) indicates manufacturing sector weakness, reducing corporate profitability and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Consumer price inflation exceeding 3.0% (CPIAUCSL > 3.0) erodes real purchasing power and increases recession risk, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3.0 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in employment (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signal severe labor market contraction, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as recession fears accelerate.
failure_condition: PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise for 2 consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 0.5% signals monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and reducing valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 0.5 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1500.0 (HOUST > 1500.0) indicate robust consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1500.0 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods.
